title: An etale rational parameter for a valued smooth function field
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed, def-weil-field], let $R\subseteq K$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$, and suppose its prime ideals form a finite chain. Let $L/K$ be a finitely generated field extension of transcendence degree one [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Let $W\subseteq L$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $L$ such that $W\cap K=R$. Here a valuation ring in a field $F$ is a subring $A$ such that for every $z\in F^\times$, either $z$ or $z^{-1}$ belongs to $A$. Put $KW=(R\setminus\{0\})^{-1}W\subseteq L$. Assume that there are a smooth integral $K$-scheme $C$ of finite type and dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], an identification of its function field $k(C)$ with $L$, and a $K$-morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(KW)\to C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] inducing this identification at the generic point. Then there is $t\in W$, transcendental over $K$, such that $L$ is finite over $F=K(t)$ and the inclusion $W\cap F\hookrightarrow W$ is etale, meaning that $\operatorname{Spec}W\to\operatorname{Spec}(W\cap F)$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The function field of an integral scheme is its local ring at the generic point.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.8 and Lemmas 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.1.6, pp. 7--10; smooth-centre formulation used in the first substantive paragraph of the proof of Proposition 4.3.3, pp. 29--30. Primary PDF read online on 2026-10-18; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: We prove the assertion by strong induction on the finite height $h$ of $R$, uniformly in all the other data, and first construct a parameter $x\in L$ without requiring $x\in W$. By [lem-trf-curve-separating-parameters] there is a separating parameter, and its bad-parameter subfield $D$ is proper. By [lem-trf-valuation-height-coarsening], $W$ has finite height at most $h+1$. For any transcendental $x$, [lem-trf-valuation-algebraic-height] also makes $W\cap K(x)$ finite-height, since $L/K(x)$ is finite. Put $A=KW$. It is a valuation overring by [lem-trf-valuation-height-coarsening]. We treat $A\ne L$ before $A=L$ at each height; the former case will not use induction.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.8, finite-height proof on printed pp. 12--13; finite height of the base is already assumed here.

proof.text: We will use the following elementary finite-height upgrade. If $V$ is a valuation ring with finitely many primes and $B$ is etale over $V$, each fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is a finite set, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product]. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is finite. For $q\in\operatorname{Spec}B$, choose for every prime $p\not\subseteq q$ an element $a_p\in p\setminus q$, and put $f=\prod a_p$ (empty product $1$). Then $D(f)$ consists exactly of the primes contained in $q$; every $s\notin q$ lies in none of these primes, so is a unit in $B_f$. Thus $B_q=B_f$. Its spectrum is an open of $\operatorname{Spec}B$, so $V\to B_q$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Consequently a localization at a prime of an etale algebra over a finite-height valuation ring is etale.

source.place: Lemma 2.1.1 and Lemma 2.1.6, printed pp. 7 and 10; explicit finite-prime localization argument.

proof.text: Suppose $A\ne L$. Apply [lem-trf-curve-centred-valuation-dvr] to the given smooth curve and the given centre of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. It gives an etale coordinate $x$, $F=K(x)$, and $O=A\cap F$ such that $L/F$ is finite separable, $O$ and $A$ are DVRs, $A$ is a localization of an etale $O$-algebra, and their residue fields are the same field $E$. Step 2 gives that $O\to A$ is etale. This uses the genuine etale coordinate from the chart, not an arbitrary uniformizer.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.8, non-bounded case, printed pp. 12--13; corrected coordinate choice from Stacks 054L.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-valuation-height-coarsening], $W$ is the inverse image of a finite-height valuation ring $W_0\subseteq E=A/\mathfrak m_A$. Restrict this description to $F$. Since $O$ has the same residue field $E$, $W\cap F$ is the inverse image of exactly the same $W_0$. Apply [lem-trf-composed-valuation-etale] to $F\subseteq L$, the etale DVR extension $O\to A$, and the identity $W_0\to W_0$. It gives $W\cap F\to W$ etale. This completes the case $A\ne L$ at every height.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.8, end of the non-bounded paragraph; Lemma 2.1.4(i) and Proposition 2.2.2.

proof.text: Now suppose $A=L$. If $h=0$, then $R=K\subseteq W$, whence $KW=W=L$. Choose a separating parameter $x$ by [lem-trf-curve-separating-parameters]. The inclusion $W\cap K(x)=K(x)\to W=L$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale]. This proves the induction base.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.8, bounded case of height zero, printed p. 13.

proof.text: For $h>0$, apply [lem-trf-valuation-height-coarsening] in the bounded case. Denote its compatible height-one valuation rings in $K,L$ by $R_1,A_1$, their residue fields by $k,E$, and their residual valuation rings by $R_0,W_0$. Thus $\operatorname{height}(R_0)=h-1$, and $R,W$ are the respective inverse images of $R_0,W_0$. Give $L$ the real absolute value supplied by [lem-trf-height-one-real-absolute-value] for $A_1$ and restrict it to $K$; the restriction is nontrivial since $R_1$ has height one. Write $\widehat K\subseteq\widehat L$ for the completions. By [lem-trf-sepclosed-rank-one-completion], $\widehat K$ and $k$ are algebraically closed.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.8, height-one coarsening paragraph, printed p. 13.

proof.text: The complement of $D$ is dense for this absolute value. Indeed choose $b\notin D$ and $c\in K$ with $0<|c|<1$. If a ball about $a$ misses $D$ it already meets the complement; if it contains $d\in D$, then $d+bc^n\notin D$ for every $n$, since $D$ is a $K$-linear subspace, and these elements tend to $d$. Thus every ball in $L$ meets $L\setminus D$. Since $L$ is dense in $\widehat L$, every ball of $\widehat L$ meets $L\setminus D$ as well. This proves exactly the density needed for perturbations.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.8, small-perturbation paragraph, printed p. 13; elementary argument replacing the source word nowhere dense by empty interior.

proof.text: Choose a separating parameter $y\in L$ using [lem-trf-curve-separating-parameters]. Since $L/K(y)$ is finite, [lem-trf-valued-decompletion-etale] makes $\widehat L$ finite over the completion of $K(y)$ inside it. This completion is the closure of $\widehat K(y)$: $K$ is dense in $\widehat K$, and rational functions in $y$ are approximated coefficientwise with nonzero denominators. Thus, if $\widehat L\ne\widehat K$, the hypotheses of [lem-trf-analytic-uniformization] apply to $\widehat L/\widehat K$.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.8, application of Theorem 2.1.10, printed p. 13.

proof.text: First suppose $E=k$. If $\widehat L=\widehat K$, choose any $x\in L\setminus D$. The closure of $K(x)$ contains the dense subfield $K$ and so equals $\widehat L$; its completed extension is the identity. If $\widehat L\ne\widehat K$, [lem-trf-analytic-uniformization] gives a parameter in $\widehat L$ and a ball on which the completed extension is finite etale on valuation rings. Step 7 supplies $x\in L\setminus D$ in that ball. In both cases $L/K(x)$ is finite separable by [lem-trf-curve-separating-parameters]. Therefore [lem-trf-valued-decompletion-etale] gives $A_1\cap K(x)\to A_1$ etale. The residue field of $A_1\cap K(x)$ is $k$ since it contains that of $R_1$ and lies in $E=k$. Its residual valuation ring and $W_0$ are both $R_0$. Apply [lem-trf-composed-valuation-etale] to obtain $W\cap K(x)\to W$ etale.

Suppose $E\ne k$. By [lem-trf-abhyankar-inequality], $\operatorname{trdeg}_kE\leq1$. Since $k$ is algebraically closed, $E\ne k$ forces $\operatorname{trdeg}_kE=1$. Choose $\bar y\in E$ transcendental over $k$ and lift it to $y\in A_1$. The residue field of $K(y)$ is $k(\bar y)$: after dividing the coefficients of a polynomial by one of largest absolute value, its nonzero reduction cannot vanish at the transcendental $\bar y$; apply this to numerator and denominator. Moreover $E/k(\bar y)$ is finite: linearly independent residues lift to $K(y)$-linearly independent elements of $L$, since dividing any proposed finite relation by a coefficient of largest absolute value and reducing would contradict residue independence. Their number is therefore bounded by $[L:K(y)]<\infty$. Thus $E/k$ is finitely generated of transcendence degree one.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.8, residually transcendental case, printed p. 13; finite-generation hypothesis for induction written explicitly.

proof.text: The ring $(R_0\setminus\{0\})^{-1}W_0$ is a valuation ring of $E$ containing $k$. By [lem-trf-algclosed-curve-model], it has a centre on a smooth integral proper curve over $k$ with field $E$. Hence all hypotheses of the induction assertion hold for $k\subseteq E$ with base valuation ring $R_0$, whose height is $h-1$. The induction hypothesis gives $\bar x\in W_0$, transcendental over $k$, such that $E/k(\bar x)$ is finite and the inclusion $W_0\cap k(\bar x)\to W_0$ is etale. This field extension is separable: base change the etale ring extension to the fraction field of its source. The resulting algebra is a domain algebraic over that field (as $E/k(\bar x)$ is finite), hence is its own fraction field $E$. Now use [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], and apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product].

source.place: Theorem 2.1.8, induction on the residual valued extension, printed p. 13; model existence is Stacks 0BY1 and 0BY3.

proof.text: Choose a lift of $\bar x$ to $A_1$. Its full set of lifts is an open ball, so Step 7 gives a lift $x\in L\setminus D$ with that same residue. By [lem-trf-curve-separating-parameters], $L/K(x)$ is finite separable. Completion preserves the residue fields by [lem-trf-valued-decompletion-etale]. Now [lem-trf-analytic-uniformization], its residue-prescribed clause, makes $\widehat L$ finite etale on valuation rings over the closure of $\widehat K(x)$. This is the completion of $K(x)$ as in Step 8. Apply [lem-trf-valued-decompletion-etale] to get $A_1\cap K(x)\to A_1$ etale.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.8, prescribed-residue application of Theorem 2.1.10(iii), then Proposition 2.2.1, printed p. 13.

proof.text: As in Step 10, the residue field of $A_1\cap K(x)$ is $k(\bar x)$. The residual valuation ring obtained by restricting $W$ to $K(x)$ is therefore $W_0\cap k(\bar x)$, by the restriction clause of [lem-trf-valuation-height-coarsening]. Its map to $W_0$ is etale by Step 11. Both have finite height, being restrictions of the finite-height valuations in Step 1 (or by [lem-trf-valuation-algebraic-height] for the finite extension $E/k(\bar x)$). Apply [lem-trf-composed-valuation-etale] to this residual extension and the coarsened etale extension of Step 12. This gives $W\cap K(x)\to W$ etale and completes the induction step.

source.place: Theorem 2.1.8, final use of Proposition 2.2.2, printed p. 13.

proof.text: In each case we have a nonzero transcendental $x$ with $L/K(x)$ finite and $W\cap K(x)\to W$ etale. If $x\in W$, take $t=x$. Otherwise the valuation-ring alternative gives $t=x^{-1}\in W$. Inversion preserves transcendence, and $K(t)=K(x)$, so neither the finite extension nor the inclusion of valuation rings changes. This gives every clause of the item.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.3, parameter paragraph, printed p. 29: replace the parameter by its inverse if necessary.
